reference_use.conclusion:
The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) holds the frozen Ch06 Contract and a byte-identical Submission with no Submission.* declarations.

SimonGMT supplies the definitions the children use: Covector; NVector; SimonMultiIndex := Fin n ↪o Fin p; wedgeCovectors with wedgeCovectors_apply_det (Simon 6.1.1); euclideanCovectorCoordinate, defined as c(fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (I j) 1); and covectorEuclideanNorm, the square root of a sum over StrictMono J : Fin n → Fin P of squared basisFun evaluations. SimonGMT has no Kronecker-duality, increasing-coordinate extensionality or coordinate-bound lemma.

The pinned Mathlib provides every tool cited in the child proofs: Module.Basis.ext_alternating, AlternatingMap.map_perm, Tuple.sort/Tuple.monotone_sort, Monotone.strictMono_of_injective, OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono, OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT, Set.ncard_range_of_injective, Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le, Matrix.one_apply/det_one/det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero, ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective, PiLp.single_apply and EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply. The proofs cite OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT and PiLp.single_apply instead of the deprecated aliases OrderEmbedding.range_inj and EuclideanSpace.single_apply.

SimonMultiIndex has a Fintype instance (RelEmbedding.instFintype) but no DecidableEq instance, so the Kronecker child is stated as an explicit conjunction.

The DAG holds two unaccepted nodes, cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge and slicing_ru_covector_expansion, whose statement equals the expansion step of this proof. That step therefore stays inline in the parent, and no accepted declaration exists to reuse. No DAG or node file reserves polyhedral_approx_pairing_{wedge_kronecker, covector_ext, coordinate_bound} or states their types.

In the scratch build of the frozen project, all three child types pass validate_lean_statement and elaborate in the comparator child scope. Complete Lean proofs of all three children compile. The selected frozen type compiles from only these children as _root_.HumanizeNodeComparator.target, with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

Simon's chapter-06.txt §1 (1.1–1.2, 1.5–1.7) states the expansion ω = Σ ω_α dx^α with ω_α = ω(e_{i1},…,e_{in}) as 'one easily checks'. The children supply exactly those checks.

rationale:
Split into three independent children. The selected statement joins two logically independent facts: the pairing identity w(c) = Σ_I c_I·w(dx^I) and the coefficient bound |c_I| ≤ |c|. Its supplied proof rests on three standard, reusable linear-algebra facts, and each child takes one of them, with a self-contained proof extracted from the supplied argument:
(a) wedge_kronecker (Step 1): Kronecker duality on increasing multi-indices, dx^I(e_I) = 1 and dx^I(e_J) = 0 for J ≠ I.
(b) covector_ext (Step 2 plus the extensionality bullet of Step 3): an n-covector on ℝ^P is determined by its increasing-basis coordinates (sorting, AlternatingMap.map_perm, Module.Basis.ext_alternating).
(c) coordinate_bound (Step 5): |c_I| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm c.
Simon compresses (a) and (b) into 'one easily checks' at 6.1.2 (book/chapter-06.txt, p. 132). The three children have no sibling dependencies and can run in parallel.

The selected node keeps only Steps 3–4. Let c′ := Σ_I c_I • dx^I. For every J, euclideanCovectorCoordinate c′ J = Σ_I c_I · euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J (ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul). By (a) and Finset.sum_eq_single this equals c_J. So (b) gives c = c′. Linearity of the continuous linear functional w (map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul) then gives w c = Σ_I c_I · w(dx^I), which is the first conjunct. The second conjunct is (c) verbatim.

The expansion c = Σ_I c_I • dx^I is deliberately not a fourth child. Up to binder names, it is the frozen statement of two unaccepted nodes in other branches, cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge and slicing_ru_covector_expansion. A separate child would duplicate another DAG node and add a serial dependency. Keeping it inline costs the parent about 15 Lean lines.

Verification was done in a scratch build of the frozen project (/tmp/pe_decomp_check_1996; project d8d46c9, Mathlib 25730c7c, pinned packages):
1. All three child types pass lean_contract.validate_lean_statement and elaborate after `import GMT.Ch06.Submission` in the comparator's contract scope, which is replayed from gmt-compare.contract_scope.
2. Complete Lean proofs of the three children compile (Scratch/Final.lean, Scratch/ThreeWay.lean). They follow exactly the numbered natural proofs given here.
3. The selected node's exact frozen type compiles as `_root_.HumanizeNodeComparator.target`, proved from only the three children by the Step 3–4 argument above.
4. Every `#print axioms` shows [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

Instance checks:
- SimonMultiIndex n P has no DecidableEq instance (`#synth` fails), so wedge_kronecker is stated as an explicit conjunction instead of `if I = J then 1 else 0`.
- The Fintype instance on SimonMultiIndex is RelEmbedding.instFintype, the same one the parent statement uses.
- `(r • c) v = r * c v` holds by rfl, so the `•` in the parent's internal expansion is the ℝ-module action that map_smul needs.

subproblems.title: Kronecker duality of coordinate wedges on increasing multi-indices (Simon 6.1.1–1.2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 be the k-th standard basis vector of ℝ^P = Eucl P. For a strictly increasing multi-index I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P), let dx^I := dx^{I(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(n−1)} = wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P). Then dx^I(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) = 1. Moreover dx^I(e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}) = 0 for every J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with J ≠ I. In the project's notation: euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I I = 1, and euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = 0 for all J ≠ I.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I : SimonMultiIndex n P), euclideanCovectorCoordinate (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))) I = 1 ∧ ∀ J : SimonMultiIndex n P, J ≠ I → euclideanCovectorCoordinate (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))) J = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (dx^I on increasing basis tuples), with details filled in.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 and proj_k := EuclideanSpace.proj k, so proj_k(y) = y_k for y ∈ E. By definition, euclideanCovectorCoordinate ω J = ω(fun j => e_{J(j)}) for ω ∈ Covector E n and J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. Fix I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. It is an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P, hence injective. Put dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => proj_{I(j)}).

1. (Matrix entries.) For a, b ∈ Fin P, proj_a(e_b) = (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)(a), which is 1 if a = b and 0 otherwise (PiLp.single_apply). Hence, for J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P and i, j ∈ Fin n, proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)}) is 1 if I(i) = J(j) and 0 otherwise.
2. (Determinant formula.) Let J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. By wedgeCovectors_apply_det (SimonGMT; Simon 6.1.1), euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = dx^I(fun j => e_{J(j)}) = det M_J, where M_J := Matrix.of (fun i j => proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)})). By Step 1, (M_J)_{ij} is 1 if I(i) = J(j) and 0 otherwise.
3. (Case J = I.) (M_I)_{ij} = 1 iff I(i) = I(j) iff i = j, because I is injective (OrderEmbedding.injective). So M_I is the identity matrix entrywise (Matrix.one_apply), and det M_I = 1 (Matrix.det_one). By Step 2, euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I I = 1. This is the first conjunct.
4. (Some row index is missing from J.) Let J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with J ≠ I. We claim some i ∈ Fin n satisfies I(i) ≠ J(j) for every j ∈ Fin n. Suppose not. Then every I(i) equals some J(j), so Set.range I ⊆ Set.range J. Since I and J are injective, Set.ncard (Set.range I) = Nat.card (Fin n) = Set.ncard (Set.range J) (Set.ncard_range_of_injective). A subset of a finite set with at least as many elements equals that set (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le; Set.range J is finite), so Set.range I = Set.range J. Two order embeddings of the well-order Fin n with the same range are equal (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so I = J. This contradicts J ≠ I.
5. (Case J ≠ I.) Take i as in Step 4. By Step 1, (M_J)_{ij} = 0 for every j ∈ Fin n, so row i of M_J is zero and det M_J = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero). By Step 2, euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = 0. Since J ≠ I was arbitrary, this is the second conjunct.
6. (Uniformity.) No case split on n or P is needed. For n = 0, M_I is the empty matrix. It equals the identity, so det M_I = 1. SimonMultiIndex 0 P has exactly one element, so the second conjunct is vacuous. For n > P, SimonMultiIndex n P is empty, so the statement is vacuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)}) is 1 if I(i) = J(j) and 0 otherwise (PiLp.single_apply), and euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J is the determinant of this matrix (wedgeCovectors_apply_det).
J = I: the matrix is the identity because I is injective, so the coordinate is det 1 = 1.
J ≠ I: if range I ⊆ range J, equal cardinalities and OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT would force I = J, so some I(i) lies outside range J.
Row i of the matrix is then zero, so the coordinate is 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).

subproblems.title: An n-covector on ℝ^P is determined by its increasing-basis coordinates (Simon 6.1.2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let α, β ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) be n-covectors, i.e. continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n). For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Suppose α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) = β(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), i.e. euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I, for every strictly increasing multi-index I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P). Then α = β.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α β : Covector (Eucl P) n), (∀ I : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I) → α = β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 (sorting injective tuples) and the extensionality bullet of Step 3 of the parent-supplied proof, with details filled in.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Let b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis be the standard basis of E; b k = e_k by EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply. By definition, euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I = γ(fun j => e_{I(j)}). Let f := α.toAlternatingMap and g := β.toAlternatingMap be the underlying alternating maps; they take the same values as α and β.

1. (Reduction to alternating maps.) A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So it suffices to prove f = g.
2. (Reduction to injective basis tuples.) By Module.Basis.ext_alternating for the basis b, it suffices to prove f(fun i => b(v i)) = g(fun i => b(v i)) for every injective v : Fin n → Fin P. Fix such an injective v.
3. (Sorting.) Let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n. By Tuple.monotone_sort, v ∘ σ is monotone. It is also injective, as a composition of the injective maps σ and v, so it is strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective). Let I := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono (v ∘ σ) ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, so I(j) = v(σ(j)) for all j ∈ Fin n. Since σ is a bijection, range I = range v. Thus I is the increasing enumeration of range v, the multi-index I_J of the parent proof's Step 2.
4. (Tuple identity.) (fun i => b(v i)) = (fun j => e_{I(j)}) ∘ σ⁻¹. Indeed, for each i ∈ Fin n, e_{I(σ⁻¹(i))} = e_{v(σ(σ⁻¹(i)))} = e_{v(i)} = b(v i).
5. (Sign rule.) Let h be an alternating map on E with arguments indexed by Fin n, u a tuple and τ a permutation of Fin n. Then h(u ∘ τ) = sign(τ) • h(u) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Apply this with u := (fun j => e_{I(j)}) and τ := σ⁻¹, and use Step 4. For γ ∈ {α, β} this gives γ(fun i => b(v i)) = sign(σ⁻¹) • γ(fun j => e_{I(j)}) = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I.
6. (Conclusion.) By hypothesis, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I. By Step 5, f(fun i => b(v i)) = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I = g(fun i => b(v i)). Since v was an arbitrary injective tuple, Step 2 gives f = g, and Step 1 gives α = β.
7. (Uniformity.) No case split is needed. For n = 0 the only v is the empty tuple, which is injective, and I is the empty embedding. For n > P there is no injective v : Fin n → Fin P, so the condition in Step 2 holds vacuously and α = β (both are 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to underlying alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective), then to injective basis tuples (Module.Basis.ext_alternating with the standard basis b, b k = e_k).
Sort an injective v: σ := Tuple.sort v makes v ∘ σ monotone and injective, hence strictly increasing; this defines I := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono (v ∘ σ) ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P.
Since (b ∘ v) = e_I ∘ σ⁻¹, AlternatingMap.map_perm gives γ(b ∘ v) = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I for γ = α and γ = β.
The coordinate hypothesis gives agreement on every injective basis tuple, hence α = β.

subproblems.title: Each increasing coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm, |c_I| ≤ |c|
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let c ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) be an n-covector (Covector (Eucl P) n), and let I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P be a strictly increasing multi-index (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P). Let c_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I = c(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), where e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Let |c| := covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S. Here S := Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} t_J, with t_J := c(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J 0), …, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J (n−1)))² if J is StrictMono and t_J := 0 otherwise. Then |c_I| ≤ |c|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (c : Covector (Eucl P) n) (I : SimonMultiIndex n P), |euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm c
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 (coordinate bound) of the parent-supplied proof, with details filled in.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Write c_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I = c(fun i => e_{I(i)}).

1. (Unfolding the norm.) By definition, covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S, where S := Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} t_J is a sum over the finite type of all maps J : Fin n → Fin P. Here t_J := (c(fun i => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J i)))² if J is StrictMono, and t_J := 0 otherwise.
2. (Nonnegativity.) Each t_J is either a square or 0, so t_J ≥ 0 for every J.
3. (The term of I.) The underlying map ⇑I : Fin n → Fin P of the order embedding I is StrictMono (OrderEmbedding.strictMono). Also EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i) = EuclideanSpace.single (I i) 1 = e_{I(i)} for every i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). Hence t_{⇑I} = (c(fun i => e_{I(i)}))² = c_I².
4. (One term is at most the sum.) A single term of a finite sum of nonnegative terms is at most the whole sum (Finset.single_le_sum, using Step 2 and ⇑I ∈ Finset.univ). Therefore c_I² = t_{⇑I} ≤ S.
5. (Square roots.) The real square root is monotone (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt), and √(x²) = |x| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs). Hence |c_I| = √(c_I²) ≤ √S = covectorEuclideanNorm c. ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S, where S = Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} t_J is a finite sum of nonnegative terms (squares or 0).
For J = ⇑I, which is StrictMono, t_J = c_I², using EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply to identify basisFun (I i) with e_{I(i)}.
